clue.text: Didn't guess right!

parts.note: a long-winded way of saying someone formed a wrong conclusion from guesswork

explanation.definitionFit: To misjudge by supposition is to have made a faulty surmise, an incorrect guess.

clue.text: Troublous enough to weary a few.

parts.note: to weary someone is to irk or tire them

explanation.surface: Something troublesome is enough to tire out a small number of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Troublous means causing trouble or annoyance, which is a synonym for tiresome or vexing.

clue.text: The answer to the con man's prayer.

definitions.text: The answer to the con man's prayer.

parts.words: The answer to the con man's prayer.
parts.note: what a swindler hopes and prays to find in a victim: a readiness to believe anything

explanation.definitionFit: Gullibility, the readiness to believe without evidence, is exactly what a swindler wants in a mark.

clue.text: Like a detective well on the scent?

definitions.text: Like a detective well on the scent?

parts.words: Like a detective well on the scent?
parts.note: a sleuth on a trail is sniffing around, as a dog follows a scent with its nose

explanation.definitionFit: Prying or sniffing about inquisitively, as a detective or hound does on a trail.

clue.text: Having gone a bit too far.

definitions.text: Having gone a bit too far.

parts.words: Having gone a bit too far.
parts.note: having overstepped a limit, gone beyond what was allowed

explanation.definitionFit: To have overstepped a limit or gone beyond a bound is to have surpassed it.

clue.text: A touch? It's in character!

definitions.meaning: a touch here is a stroke or slight trace, as in a touch of humour
a distinguishing quality that forms part of someone's character

explanation.definitionFit: A characteristic feature of a person, and in an older sense a stroke or touch of the pen.

clue.text: Certainly not steady progress.

parts.note: the movement of someone staggering or lurching from side to side, the opposite of a steady gait

explanation.definitionFit: Staggering or swaying unsteadily as one moves along, like a drunk.

clue.text: A pair of zebras — an unexpected take-in!

definitions.meaning: a zebra is a striped pedestrian crossing in Britain, so two of them make two crossings
a take-in is a deception, here a betrayal by someone trusted

explanation.walkthrough: A zebra crossing is the British black-and-white striped pedestrian crossing, so 'a pair of zebras' is literally two crossings.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying a partner after pretending to cooperate is a treacherous deception; two zebra crossings also make the phrase literally.

clue.text: Vainer attempts perhaps — still, he has to work on hard material.

definitions.text: he has to work on hard material

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of vainer attempts might be arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Someone's conceited efforts are dismissed, while a craftsman toils on tough stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange VAINER ATTEMPTS (signalled by 'perhaps'). The definition is cryptic: such an artist chalks pictures on paving stones, a hard surface; 'still' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A street painter who draws chalk pictures on the paving stones, a hard surface, for passers-by.

clue.text: They may, be found around a low joint.

definitions.text: They may, be found around a low joint.

parts.words: They may, be found around a low joint.
parts.note: ornaments worn encircling the lowest joint of the leg, just above the foot

explanation.definitionFit: Bands or chains worn as jewellery round the joint between leg and foot.

clue.text: Fine place this for French wine.

definitions.text: Fine place this for French wine.

parts.words: Fine place this for French wine.
parts.note: a grand French country house, and also the estate whose name is given to a Bordeaux wine

explanation.definitionFit: A French country mansion; Bordeaux wines are named after the estate where they are made.

clue.text: In the course of which one may be

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'In the course of which one may be (5)': the clue is cut short after 'may be' and no scan gives the rest.
annotationWithheld.clue: In the course of which one may be

clue.text: A pupil's cover-up, when down?

parts.note: the pupil is that of the eye, and its cover is lowered over it when one blinks or sleeps

explanation.definitionFit: The fold of skin that closes over the eye, hiding the pupil when lowered.

clue.text: Fancy, Alec's pig like a prehistoric Greek!

indicators.note: fancy as an imperative invites the solver to imagine the letters of the next words in a new shape

parts.note: the letters of these two words, the possessive's S included

explanation.surface: Imagine a man's pig resembling some ancient Hellenic figure!
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'Fancy' is the anagram signal, not an adjective. The S of 'Alec's' counts as a letter of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pelasgians were the pre-Hellenic people said to have lived in Greece before the classical Greeks.

clue.text: Physical insensibility produced wild Asian gale.

indicators.note: wild describes the letters of the two words running riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A fierce storm from Asia knocked people senseless.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of the ability to feel pain is a medical form of bodily numbness.

clue.text: ship!

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'ship! (8)': the clue is cut short, only its last word survives, and no scan gives the rest.

clue.text: It's by no means confined to sense.

definitions.text: It's by no means confined to sense.

parts.words: It's by no means confined to sense.
parts.note: something that does not stay within sense is non-sense, silly talk

explanation.definitionFit: Tommyrot is old slang for foolish talk, utter drivel, the opposite of sense.

clue.text: Alarming result of uncommon sternutation !

indicators.note: of says the result is drawn out of the following words, which hold it inside them

explanation.surface: A rare sneeze can have frightening consequences!
explanation.walkthrough: Sternutation is a formal word for sneezing; the answer straddles 'uncommon' and 'sternutation'.
explanation.definitionFit: A frightening creature or freak is a thing that alarms, the alarming product of some process.

clue.text: Pampas cowboy, not entirely socially.

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'Pampas cowboy, not entirely socially.': GAUCH(E) needs an O and a word for socially awkward that the clue as held lacks, so the clue looks cut short and no scan gives the rest.

clue.text: "The land of lost shining plain" (Housman).

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'The land of lost shining plain (Housman)': the quotation ('That is the land of lost content, I see it shining plain') is cut short and no scan gives the printed text.

clue.text: More land — it's simply ideal!

parts.note: Sir Thomas More wrote of an imaginary island with a perfect society

explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's imaginary island of a perfect society, hence any ideal place.

clue.text: Rows in classes.

definitions.meaning: rows here are lines of people or things side by side
classes are grades or levels in a hierarchy, as in social standing

explanation.definitionFit: Lines of soldiers standing side by side; also grades of social or military standing.

clue.text: Suitable salary for a stingy fellow.

definitions.text: Suitable salary for a stingy fellow.

parts.words: Suitable salary for a stingy fellow.
parts.note: the same slang word means both wages and a miser, so the pay suits the man

explanation.definitionFit: Old slang for wages, and also for a mean miserly person, so the pay matches the skinflint.

clue.text: They are sure to turn up in a suit.

definitions.text: They are sure to turn up in a suit.

parts.words: They are sure to turn up in a suit.
parts.note: a suit is a lawsuit, and the parties to it must appear in court

explanation.definitionFit: The parties to a lawsuit, who must appear when the case is heard.

clue.text: All the hideous dream "(J. Caesar).

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'All the hideous dream (J. Caesar)': the Julius Caesar quotation ('all the interim is like a phantasma or a hideous dream') is cut short and no scan gives the printed text.

clue.text: Here's Dad's fowl — a leggy portion!

parts.note: Pa is a familiar word for father, with its possessive S

explanation.surface: Presenting father's bird, a portion with plenty of leg!
explanation.walkthrough: The pastern is the part of a horse's leg between fetlock and hoof, so it is literally a portion of leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The pastern is a section of a horse's leg, just above the hoof.

clue.text: Wrestler's idea of giving

parts.note: a wrestler hurls opponents, so his way of hosting a social occasion would be to hurl it

explanation.definitionFit: Throwing is the everyday idiom for hosting a party, and also what a wrestler does to opponents.
